questions.stem: State the name for the breakdown and shedding of the uterine lining.
questions.modelAnswer: The breakdown and shedding of the uterine lining is called menstruation.

questions.stem: State the day on which an egg is released and the tube it travels along.
questions.modelAnswer: An egg is released around day 14 and rides the fallopian tube toward the uterus.

questions.stem: Explain why the uterine lining thickens before ovulation rather than after menstruation only.
questions.modelAnswer: The rebuilt lining is the landing site a fertilised egg would need, so it must be ready by the time the day-14 egg could implant.

questions.modelAnswer: Progesterone stays low from day 1 to 14 and climbs after ovulation.

questions.stem: State the two effects of rising oestrogen before the egg is released.
questions.modelAnswer: Oestrogen causes the uterine wall to thicken and the egg to mature.

questions.stem: Explain why a fall in progesterone leads to menstruation.
questions.modelAnswer: Progesterone maintains the thickened uterine lining, so when its levels fall the lining loses that support and breaks down as menstruation.

questions.stem: A hormone test on day 20 shows high progesterone. What does this indicate about the cycle stage and the lining?
questions.modelAnswer: Day 20 sits after ovulation, so high progesterone shows the second half of the cycle is under way and the uterine lining is thickened and maintained.
